chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man has a deposit (trust) and a debt, and he cannot reach/access them, then he takes them. When does the obligation of zakat fall upon him? He said: 'When he takes them, and then a full year passes over him, he pays zakat.'

key_terms.الْحَوْلُ: A full lunar year of possession
key_terms.الْوَدِيعَةُ: Deposit or trust held by another

ai.seo_question: When does zakat become due on a debt or deposit that is currently inaccessible?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that for inaccessible debts or deposits, the zakat clock starts only upon actual receipt, a ruling that alleviates the burden on individuals during periods of financial uncertainty. This principle is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between nominal wealth and accessible liquidity, ensuring zakat is levied only when the owner has full control over the asset.
